title: Bug: [dualtor][vpp] Mux drop ACL ignores SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS — a single standby port blackholes the data plane on ALL ports
author: lolyu
body:
> **Note:** this issue originally reported the symptom as a possible drop-counter attribution problem, scoped to one test case. Investigation disproved that and found a far more severe root cause. The body below has been rewritten to lead with the confirmed finding; the full investigation trail is preserved in the comments.

Tracked under umbrella issue #26046. This is gap **(1)** of #28884, which was closed with only gap (2) fixed.

### Is it platform specific

vpp

### Importance or Severity

**High.** On a dual-ToR VPP deployment, a single mux port entering standby blackholes **all** data-plane traffic on **every** port of the switch. The box continues to look healthy — BGP stays up and mux HWSTATUS reads `consistent` — so the failure is silent.

### Description of the bug

`vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp` never reads `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS`. Because MuxOrch uses that attribute as the *only* mechanism scoping the mux drop ACL to standby ports, the rule degrades from "deny on the standby ports" to "deny on every bound port".

**How MuxOrch scopes the drop.** It creates a single shared table and a single shared rule for all mux ports, then edits `IN_PORTS` on each switchover (`orchagent/muxorch.cpp`):

```cpp
// port goes STANDBY -> add to IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port, RULE_OPER_ADD);

// port goes ACTIVE -> remove from IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port_, RULE_OPER_DELETE);

// last standby port leaves -> delete the rule outright
if ((port_set.size() == 1) && (port_set[0] == port_))
    gAclOrch->removeAclRule(table_name, rule_name);
```

Binding the *table* to all 32 ports is intentional and VPP honours it correctly. The bug is purely that the per-entry `IN_PORTS` qualifier is discarded:

| Layer | Intended scope | VPP behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Table -> port binding | all 32 ports (by design) | honoured |
| Entry `IN_PORTS` | standby ports only | **silently discarded** |

**The code path.** `acl_rule_field_update()` has no case for `IN_PORTS`, so it hits `default:`:

```cpp
sai_status_t status;
status = SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS;      // initialised to success

switch (attr_id) {
    /* SRC_IP, DST_IP, ICMP, L4 ports, IP_PROTOCOL, TCP_FLAGS,
       PACKET_ACTION, PRIORITY, ADMIN_STATE ... */
default:
    SWSS_LOG_ERROR("Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: %d", attr_id);
    break;                        // status still SUCCESS
}
return status;                    // returns SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS
```

It logs an error, then returns success — so orchagent believes the rule was programmed correctly and never retries or reports a fault.

`SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` = `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_START + 0xa` = `0x100a` = **4106**, and the DUT logs the miss at exactly the mux switchover time:

```
2026 Aug 18 11:13:34.709047 vlab-vpp-03 ERR syncd#syncd: :- acl_rule_field_update: Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: 4106
```

(`show mux status` reports `LAST_SWITCHOVER_TIME 2026-Aug-18 11:13:34`.)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Dual-ToR VPP KVM testbed, mux ports on `Vlan1000`.
2. Put a **single** mux port into standby: `config mux mode standby Ethernet8`.
3. Send data-plane traffic through any **other**, still-active mux port.
4. All traffic is dropped on ingress; RX_DRP climbs on the active port.

Inspect:

```bash
redis-cli -n 1 hget ASIC_STATE:SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY:<oid> SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS
docker exec syncd vppctl show acl-plugin acl
sudo grep -a "Unhandled ACL entry attribute" /var/log/syslog
```

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

**Actual** — SONiC requests the deny on 1 port; VPP applies it to all 32:

```
ASIC_DB: SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS = "1:oid:0x1000000000034"   -> Ethernet8  (1 port)

VPP:     acl-index 3  ipv4 deny src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/0
         applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32                        (32 ports)
```

**Expected** — the deny applies only to `Ethernet8`; all other ports forward normally.

### Blast radius: the failure is binary, not proportional

Because MuxOrch removes the rule entirely once the last standby port leaves, the switch has only two states. Demonstrated live on `vlab-vpp-03`:

**One port standby (`Ethernet8`):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 deny src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/0
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32          <- entire data plane dead
```

**After `config mux mode active Ethernet8` (zero standby):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 permit src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/32     <- no-op placeholder, traffic flows
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32
```

So: **no port standby → everything works; any port standby → nothing works.** One switchover on one port takes out all 24 mux ports plus the 8 non-mux ports. This is why the dualtor_io results looked erratic — runs that kept every port active passed, and any run that put a single port into standby lost everything.

### Measured impact

From `tests/logs/08181110` (`test_normal_op_active_server_to_standby_server`), with only `Ethernet8` standby:

```json
{ "sent_packets": 5721, "received_packets": 0, "received_packet_diff": -5721 }
```
```
ERROR tests.common.dualtor.dual_tor_io: Sniffer failed to filter any traffic from DUT
```

Source server `192.168.0.25` sits behind `Ethernet96`, which was **active**:

```
Address       MacAddress         Iface         Vlan
192.168.0.25  1e:e7:85:0b:70:18  Ethernet96    1000
```

`portstat` — every other mux port sits at the RX_DRP 15 baseline; `Ethernet96` is the lone outlier at 5,736. Excess `5,736 - 15 = 5,721`, an exact match for `sent_packets`.

### Why the earlier #28884 fixes did not cover this

sonic-platform-vpp#272 (merged 2026-08-11) and sonic-sairedis#2029 (merged 2026-08-17) added an ip2me / receive-DPO bypass so **control-plane** packets escape the deny. That restored heartbeat/ARP/BGP, which is why mux ports reach `consistent` and the box looks healthy — and is precisely why this is easy to miss. **Data-plane** traffic has no such bypass. sonic-sairedis#2027 (`Permit local traffic ahead of ACL deny rules`) was closed unmerged.

Note the image under test (`master-29031.1192809`, built 2026-08-14) also predates the sonic-sairedis#2029 merge.

### Suggested fix

In `vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp`:

1. Handle `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` in `acl_rule_field_update()` — resolve the `objlist` of port OIDs to hwif names.
2. Bind the deny only to those interfaces rather than every interface the table is bound to, and rebind on each `IN_PORTS` update, since MuxOrch rewrites it on every switchover.
3. Make the `default:` case return a failure status for unhandled **match/field** attributes instead of `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so a silently mis-programmed ACL surfaces as an error. Worth doing independently of the mux case — any future unhandled match field will degrade the same silent way.

### Output of `show version`

```
SONiC Software Version: SONiC.master-29031.1192809-6c879a32d
Build commit: 6c879a32d
Build date: Fri Aug 14 10:25:54 UTC 2026
Platform: x86_64-kvm_x86_64-r0
HwSKU: Force10-S6000
ASIC: vpp
```

Testbed `vms-kvm-dual-vpp-t0-1`, DUTs `vlab-vpp-03` / `vlab-vpp-04`, `active-standby` mode.

### Related

- #28884 — closed, but only gap (2) was fixed; this is gap (1)
- #29078 — same root cause, data-plane symptom
- #26046 — umbrella

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
## Correction: root cause found — my earlier counter-attribution hypothesis was wrong

The original report suggested the RX_DRP might be **counter attribution** (VPP counting by-design mux drops as `IF_IN_DISCARDS`). **That hypothesis is disproven.** The drops are real traffic loss, and the "32 ports instead of 24" observation was an understatement of a more fundamental bug.

### The real bug: `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` is never read

Reproduced on `vlab-vpp-03` with **only one** mux port standby (`Ethernet8`), all other 23 active.

SONiC programmed the drop ACL scoped to exactly **1 port**:

```
ASIC_STATE:SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY:oid:0x8000000000721
  SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_ACTION_PACKET_ACTION = SAI_PACKET_ACTION_DROP
  SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS       = "1:oid:0x1000000000034"   -> Ethernet8
```

VPP applied it to **all 32 physical ports**:

```
acl-index 3 count 1 tag {sonic_acl_oid:0x700000002}
      0: ipv4 deny src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/0 proto 0 sport 0 dport 0
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1, 2, 3, ... 32     (= bobm0..bobm31, ALL ports)
```

So the scoping is not "32 vs 24" — it is **1 requested vs 32 applied**. `IN_PORTS` is ignored entirely, and the rule degrades to an unscoped `deny any/any` on every port, **including active ones**.

Confirmed in source: `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` does not appear anywhere in `vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp` (it exists only in `SAI/inc/saiacl.h` and unit tests).

### Impact: this causes real data-plane loss on ACTIVE ports

`show mux status` at the time — `Ethernet96` is **active**:

```
Ethernet8   standby   standby   unhealthy  consistent
Ethernet96  active    active    unhealthy  consistent
```

`portstat` on the same box, with `Ethernet96` carrying the test traffic:

```
 IFACE       RX_OK    RX_DRP
 Ethernet4   1,121    15          <- baseline
 ...
 Ethernet92  1,115    15          <- baseline
 Ethernet96  6,842    5,736       <- outlier
```

Excess over baseline: RX_OK `6,842 - 1,120 = 5,722`, RX_DRP `5,736 - 15 = 5,721`.

The concurrently-running `test_normal_op_active_server_to_standby_server` reported:

```json
{
    "sent_packets": 5721,
    "received_packets": 0,
    "received_packet_diff": -5721
}
```

`5,721` sent, `5,721` dropped on `Ethernet96`, `0` received — an exact match. Every packet that entered the active port was denied by the mis-scoped ACL.

### Relationship to #28884

#28884 documented this precisely as gap **(1)**: *"VPP ignores `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` ... the rule degrades to a wildcard `ipv4 deny src 0/0 dst 0/0` applied to every bound mux port — including active ports."*

That issue was closed on 2026-08-11, but the merged work addressed gap **(2)** (the ip2me / control-plane punt ordering):

- sonic-platform-vpp#272 — merged 2026-08-11 — `[sonic_ext] Add ip2me receive-DPO ACL-bypass feature node`
- sonic-sairedis#2029 — merged 2026-08-17 — `[vpp] Drive sonic_ext ip2me ACL-bypass from drop-ACL port binds`
- sonic-sairedis#2027 — **closed unmerged** — `[vpp] Permit local traffic ahead of ACL deny rules`

Those restore **control-plane** traffic (heartbeat/ARP/BGP), which is why mux ports now reach `consistent` HWSTATUS. But none of them make the ACL honour `IN_PORTS`, so **data-plane** traffic on active ports is still dropped. Gap (1) was never fixed.

Note the image under test (`master-29031.1192809`, built 2026-08-14) also predates the sonic-sairedis#2029 merge (2026-08-17).

Suggest either reopening #28884 for gap (1) or tracking it here.

### Consequences for the other filed issues

- #29078 (`test_normal_op_active_server_to_standby_server`) has the **same root cause** and is not a tunnel/routing problem. The evidence above is from that exact test run.
- The `test_upstream_standby_rx_drop_check` failure originally reported here is the same mechanism observed on a standby-heavy configuration.

### Suggested fix

Implement `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` in `vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp` so the deny is bound only to the ports listed in the entry, and re-evaluated when MuxOrch rewrites the list on switchover.

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
## Full mechanism — and an important correction to the "32 vs 24 ports" framing

Additional investigation has pinned the exact code path, confirmed it from the live DUT's own logs, and revealed that the blast radius is far wider than first reported.

**Correction:** my earlier note called the 32-port table binding "a separately verified fidelity bug." **That was wrong.** Binding the ACL *table* to all mux ports is intentional SONiC design. The one and only bug is that the per-entry `IN_PORTS` qualifier is discarded.

### How MuxOrch actually scopes the drop

MuxOrch does **not** create one ACL per standby port. It creates a **single** table and a **single** rule shared by every mux port, and then uses `IN_PORTS` as the sole discriminator between active and standby (`orchagent/muxorch.cpp`):

```cpp
// port goes STANDBY -> add it to the rule's IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port, RULE_OPER_ADD);

// port goes ACTIVE -> remove it from IN_PORTS
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port_, RULE_OPER_DELETE);

// last standby port leaves -> delete the rule outright
vector<sai_object_id_t> port_set = rule->getInPorts();
if ((port_set.size() == 1) && (port_set[0] == port_))
{
    gAclOrch->removeAclRule(table_name, rule_name);
}
```

Confirmed on the DUT — all 32 ports carry `SAI_PORT_ATTR_INGRESS_ACL`, which is correct and intended:

```
ports with INGRESS_ACL set: 32
ACL_TABLE_GROUP_MEMBER entries: 64
```

So the split of responsibility is:

| Layer | Scope | VPP behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Table -> port binding | all 32 ports (by design) | honoured correctly |
| Entry `IN_PORTS` qualifier | only the standby ports | **silently discarded** |

`IN_PORTS` is not a hint or an optimisation — it is the *entire* mechanism separating a standby port from an active one. Drop it and the deny becomes unconditional on every bound port.

### The exact code path

`vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp`, `acl_rule_field_update()` — the switch has no case for `IN_PORTS`, so it falls to `default:`:

```cpp
sai_status_t status;
status = SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS;      // <-- initialised to success

switch (attr_id) {
    /* ... SRC_IP, DST_IP, ICMP, L4 ports, IP_PROTOCOL, TCP_FLAGS,
           PACKET_ACTION, PRIORITY, ADMIN_STATE ... */

default:
    SWSS_LOG_ERROR("Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: %d", attr_id);
    break;                        // <-- falls through, status still SUCCESS
}

return status;                    // <-- returns SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS
```

It logs an error and then **returns success**. orchagent therefore believes the rule was programmed exactly as requested and never retries or reports a failure. The rule silently degrades from *"deny on the standby ports"* to *"deny on everything."*

`SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` = `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_START + 0xa` = `0x100a` = **4106**. The DUT's own syslog records the miss, timed exactly to the mux switchover in `show mux status` (`LAST_SWITCHOVER_TIME 2026-Aug-18 11:13:34`):

```
2026 Aug 18 11:11:30.567114 vlab-vpp-03 ERR syncd#syncd: :- acl_rule_field_update: Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: 4106
2026 Aug 18 11:13:34.709047 vlab-vpp-03 ERR syncd#syncd: :- acl_rule_field_update: Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: 4106
```

### Blast radius: ONE standby port blackholes ALL 32 ports

Because MuxOrch deletes the rule entirely when the last standby port leaves, the failure is binary rather than proportional. Demonstrated live on `vlab-vpp-03`:

**With exactly one port standby (`Ethernet8`):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 deny src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/0
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32          <- ALL ports blackholed
```

**After `config mux mode active Ethernet8` (zero standby):**
```
acl-index 3  ipv4 permit src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/32     <- no-op placeholder, traffic flows
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1 .. 32
```

So the switch has only two states: **no port standby → everything works**, or **any port standby → the entire data plane is dead**. A single mux switchover on one port takes out all 24 mux ports plus the 8 non-mux ports.

This also explains why the failure looked intermittent across the test suite. Tests that happened to run with all ports active passed; any test that put even one port into standby lost everything.

### Confirmed end to end

`192.168.0.25` — the source server for the failing test — is behind `Ethernet96`, which was **active** at the time:

```
Address       MacAddress         Iface         Vlan
192.168.0.25  1e:e7:85:0b:70:18  Ethernet96    1000
```

```
Ethernet8   standby  ...        <- the only standby port
Ethernet96  active   ...        <- source server ingress, still blackholed
```

`portstat`: every other mux port sits at RX_DRP 15 (baseline); `Ethernet96` shows 5,736. Excess `5,736 - 15 = 5,721`, matching `sent_packets: 5721 / received_packets: 0` exactly.

### Why the earlier #28884 fixes did not help

sonic-platform-vpp#272 and sonic-sairedis#2029 added an ip2me / receive-DPO bypass so **control-plane** packets escape the deny. That is why mux ports now reach `consistent` HWSTATUS and BGP stays up — and why the breakage is easy to miss, since the box looks healthy. **Data-plane** traffic has no such bypass and is still dropped on every port.

### Suggested fix

In `vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp`:

1. Handle `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` in `acl_rule_field_update()` — resolve the `objlist` of port OIDs to hwif names.
2. Bind the deny only to those interfaces instead of every interface the table is bound to, and rebind on every `IN_PORTS` update (MuxOrch rewrites it on each switchover).
3. Change the `default:` case to return a failure status for unhandled **match/field** attributes rather than `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so a silently mis-programmed ACL surfaces as an error instead of a wide-open deny. This class of bug should never again be invisible to orchagent.

Point 3 matters independently of the mux case — any future unhandled match field will degrade the same silent way.

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
## Provenance: this is a day-1 issue, not a regression — and the suggested fix needs correcting

### Day 1, confirmed across both repos' full history

`SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` has **never** been handled by the VPP SAI ACL implementation, going back to the very first ACL commit in 2023:

```
$ git log --all --oneline -S 'SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS' -- vslib/
(no results)
```

The original implementation — `f351116` (2023-07-04, *"Fixes issue #54 - Basic ACL provisioning in SONiC-VPP"*, sonic-platform-vpp) — did not handle it, and neither has any revision since. The code moved to sonic-sairedis in `552cc66c` (2025-04-14, #1473) unchanged in this respect.

Notably, the original `default:` case was **completely silent**:

```cpp
// 552cc66c (2025-04-14) and earlier
default:
    break;          // no log at all
```

The `SWSS_LOG_ERROR("Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID: %d")` seen today was only added in `b70dfa75` (2025-12-08, #1599). So the visibility of this bug has only ever improved — it was never better-behaved in the past.

### Timeline — progressively mitigated, never regressed

| Date | Commit | Effect on this bug |
|---|---|---|
| 2023-07-04 | `f351116` platform-vpp | First ACL impl. `IN_PORTS` unhandled, `default: break;` silent. **Bug born here.** |
| 2025-04-14 | `552cc66c` sairedis #1473 | Code merged to sonic-sairedis. No change in behaviour. |
| 2025-12-08 | `b70dfa75` #1599 | Adds `SWSS_LOG_ERROR` for unhandled attrs — still returns SUCCESS. First visibility. |
| 2026-08-11/12 | platform-vpp#272, sairedis#2029 | ip2me bypass restores **control plane**. Box now looks healthy. |
| 2026-08-13 | `63058c0f` | Stale deny cleared when last standby leaves. |
| today | — | **Data-plane drop on active ports still present.** |

Two of those entries deserve emphasis, because they explain why this surfaced now rather than earlier:

**Before `63058c0f` (2026-08-13) the bug was strictly worse — it was sticky.** That commit's own message describes the prior behaviour: when a table lost its last rule, `AclTblConfig()` skipped reprogramming and *"left the previously programmed VPP ACL (e.g. deny 0/0 -> 0/0) still bound to the interface."* So historically, once any port went standby, the wildcard deny persisted **even after every port returned to active**. The recovery-on-all-active behaviour I measured is new as of five days ago.

**The degradation was already documented at the time of the gap-(2) fix.** platform-vpp#272's `ip2me_node.c` states it outright:

> *Motivating case (dual-ToR mux). MuxOrch installs an ingress drop ACL scoped to the standby mux ports via `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS`. VPP's ACL plugin has no in-port packet-match field, so the rule degrades to a port-wide "ipv4 deny 0/0 -> 0/0", which drops even the ICMP mux heartbeat to the SoC loopback at l2-input.*

The known degradation was mitigated for control-plane traffic only; the data-plane consequence was not addressed. That is exactly gap (1) of #28884.

**Conclusion: day-1 issue.** No bisect target exists and no revert will help. It was latent for as long as dual-ToR was not exercised on VPP, and is only now visible because the control-plane fixes let the mux reach a healthy-looking state where data-plane traffic is actually expected to flow.

### Correction to the suggested fix

My earlier suggestion said to handle `IN_PORTS` inside `acl_rule_field_update()`. **That is not implementable as written,** and the comment quoted above is right about why. `vpp_acl_rule_t` (`vslib/vpp/vppxlate/SaiVppXlate.h`) is a pure 5-tuple match with no port member:

```c
typedef struct _vpp_acl_rule {
    vpp_acl_action_e action;
    vpp_ip_addr_t src_prefix, src_prefix_mask;
    vpp_ip_addr_t dst_prefix, dst_prefix_mask;
    int proto;
    uint16_t srcport_or_icmptype_first, srcport_or_icmptype_last;
    uint16_t dstport_or_icmpcode_first, dstport_or_icmpcode_last;
    uint8_t tcp_flags_mask, tcp_flags_value;
} vpp_acl_rule_t;
```

This mirrors upstream VPP's ACL plugin, where ingress-port scoping is expressed by **which interfaces an ACL is bound to**, never by a match field. So there is nowhere in the rule struct for `IN_PORTS` to land, and the fix has to happen at the binding layer:

1. Capture `IN_PORTS` where the ACE is processed (`fill_acl_rules()` / the `AclTblConfig()` path) rather than in `acl_rule_field_update()`, resolving the `objlist` of port OIDs to hwif names and storing it on the ACE.
2. Partition the table's entries by their `IN_PORTS` set and program **one VPP ACL per distinct set**, binding each only to its own interfaces — instead of one ACL bound to every interface the table touches. Entries with no `IN_PORTS` keep today's bind-to-all behaviour.
3. Recompute those binds whenever `IN_PORTS` is updated, since MuxOrch rewrites the list on every switchover.
4. Independently: make `default:` return a failure status for unhandled **match/field** attributes instead of `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so a silently mis-programmed ACL surfaces as an error rather than a wide-open deny.

Item 4 is worth doing regardless of how 1–3 are implemented — it is the reason this went unnoticed for over two years.

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
## Addendum: VPP *does* support ingress-port scoping — just not as a rule field. Refined fix.

I checked this against upstream VPP (`src/plugins/acl/`) and against the running DUT, because it determines whether a fix is even possible. Summary: **the capability exists, at the binding layer.** The SAI→VPP mapping is what's broken, not VPP.

### 1. VPP has no in-port *match field* — confirmed upstream

`src/plugins/acl/acl_types.api`, the `acl_rule` type in its entirety:

```c
typedef acl_rule {
  vl_api_acl_action_t is_permit;
  vl_api_prefix_t src_prefix;
  vl_api_prefix_t dst_prefix;
  vl_api_ip_proto_t proto;
  u16 srcport_or_icmptype_first, srcport_or_icmptype_last;
  u16 dstport_or_icmpcode_first, dstport_or_icmpcode_last;
  u8 tcp_flags_mask, tcp_flags_value;
};
```

The internal form (`types.h: acl_rule_t`) is identical, and the runtime match key (`fa_node.h: fa_5tuple_t`) is IPs + L4 ports/flags + `fa_packet_info_t`. No interface field anywhere. `vpp_acl_rule_t` in `SaiVppXlate.h` is a faithful 1:1 mirror — so the gap is inherited from VPP's data model, not introduced by the SONiC layer.

**This is why adding a `case SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS:` to `acl_rule_field_update()` cannot work** — that function's only output is a `vpp_acl_rule_t`, and there is no member to write to.

### 2. VPP scopes by *binding*, and the scope is resolved before rule matching

Each `(sw_if_index, direction)` owns an **ACL lookup context** (`acl.h: input_lc_index_by_sw_if_index` / `output_lc_index_by_sw_if_index`), and each context holds an **ordered vector of ACL indices** (`lookup_context.h: acl_lookup_context_t.acl_indices`). The context index is part of the packet match key itself (`fa_packet_info_t.lc_index`), so "which ACLs apply to this port" is answered *before* any rule is evaluated.

Binding is set via `acl_interface_add_del` (`sw_if_index`, `is_input`, `acl_index`) or `acl_interface_set_acl_list`. The same ACL index may be bound to any subset of interfaces.

So `IN_PORTS = {p1, p2}` is expressible — as *"bind this ACL to p1 and p2"* rather than *"match if in-port ∈ {p1,p2}"*. Semantically equivalent for the mux case; structurally different.

### 3. The mismatch is one of cardinality

| | scope carrier | granularity |
|---|---|---|
| SAI | `IN_PORTS` on the **ACL entry** | per-entry — entries in one table may differ |
| VPP | interface **binding** of the **ACL** | per-ACL — all rules share the binding |

A SAI table whose entries carry *heterogeneous* `IN_PORTS` therefore cannot be represented by a single VPP ACL. Today the code always emits exactly one VPP ACL per SAI table and binds it to every port the table touches, which silently widens every entry's scope to the union. For the mux table — one `deny any/any` entry scoped to the standby ports — that union is all 32 ports.

### 4. Live structure on the DUT, and an important mitigating detail

VPP's ACL is **implicit-deny** (`dataplane_node.c:463` `action = 0; /* deny by default */`, then `next[0] = action ? next[0] : 0;` where `0` is drop). SAI is implicit-permit. The existing code already reconciles this with a catch-all ACL bound everywhere:

```
acl-index 1 count 2 tag {sonic_acl_default_permit}
          0: ipv4 permit src 0.0.0.0/0 dst 0.0.0.0/0 ...
          1: ipv6 permit src ::/0 dst ::/0 ...
  applied inbound on sw_if_index: 1..32, 65..68
```

and per interface the list is ordered with that permit **last**:

```
$ vppctl show acl-plugin interface sw_if_index 25     # Ethernet96
sw_if_index 25:
  input acl(s): 2, 3, 1
```

`3` is the mux table's ACL, evaluated ahead of the `1` safety net — which is precisely why its `deny 0/0 -> 0/0` blackholed the port.

**This materially de-risks the fix:** because `sonic_acl_default_permit` is already bound to every interface as a tail, simply *not* binding a scoped ACL to a port is safe — the port falls through to permit rather than to VPP's implicit deny.

### 5. Refined fix

1. Capture `IN_PORTS` where the ACE is built (`fill_acl_rules()` / `AclTblConfig()` path), resolving the `objlist` of port OIDs to sw_if_indexes and storing it alongside the ACE — **not** in `acl_rule_field_update()`.
2. Partition a table's entries by their distinct `IN_PORTS` set; emit **one VPP ACL per partition**. Entries with no `IN_PORTS` keep today's bind-to-all behaviour.
3. Bind each partition's ACL only to its own interfaces, ahead of `sonic_acl_default_permit` in each interface's list. Ports not in any partition are simply left unbound for that table.
4. Recompute bindings whenever `IN_PORTS` changes — MuxOrch rewrites the list on every switchover.
5. Independently, make the `default:` case return failure for unhandled **match/field** attributes instead of `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS`, so a mis-programmed ACL surfaces as an error rather than as a silent wildcard deny.

For the mux table specifically this collapses to a single partition — one ACL bound only to the standby ports — so the common case is not expensive.

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
## Why the drop ACL lands on *every* port: it is MuxOrch's design, and `IN_PORTS` is its only safety catch

Follow-up to the analysis above. This comment answers a question that kept coming up — *"why is the drop ACL bound to all 32 ports in the first place?"* — because the answer changes what a correct fix looks like, and rules out an obvious-but-wrong one.

**Short version: the all-ports binding is intentional and correct in MuxOrch. 100% of the per-port scoping is delegated to `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS`. Dropping that one attribute therefore does not degrade the feature — it inverts it.**

I also have direct dataplane counter evidence now, and a characterisation of the failure that explains why it is easy to miss in testing.

---

### 1. MuxOrch binds to all PHY ports on purpose

`MuxAclHandler::createMuxAclTable()` ends in `bindAllPorts()` (`orchagent/muxorch.cpp:1553`):

```cpp
void MuxAclHandler::bindAllPorts(AclTable &acl_table)          // :1578
{
    auto allPorts = gPortsOrch->getAllPorts();
    for (auto &it: allPorts)
    {
        Port port = it.second;
        if (port.m_type == Port::PHY)                          // :1586
        {
            acl_table.link(port.m_port_id);
            acl_table.bind(port.m_port_id);
        }
        else if (port.m_type == Port::LAG && !is_ingress_acl_)  // :1593
        { ... }
    }
}
```

This is sound design:

* The table is created **once**, by whichever mux port goes standby first — `createMuxAclTable()` early-returns if it already exists (`:1539-1544`). At that moment it cannot know which of the other ports will go standby later, so it binds to all of them up front.
* Rebinding 32 ports on every mux transition would be expensive and racy in a failover path.
* So MuxOrch splits static from dynamic: **the binding is static and deliberately over-broad; all the dynamism lives in one rule's `IN_PORTS` list.**

Note this fires at boot: the `MuxCable` constructor defaults to standby (`:475-480`, `stateStandby()`), so the table and its 32 bindings exist from initialisation onward.

### 2. There is exactly ONE rule, and `IN_PORTS` is its only scoping mechanism

A single rule (`MUX_ACL_RULE_NAME`) is created at priority 999 with action DROP (`:1556-1576`), and every standby port adds *itself* to that same rule's port list:

```cpp
gAclOrch->updateAclRule(table_name, rule_name, MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port, RULE_OPER_ADD);      // :1505
```

Going active removes itself again, deleting the rule outright only when the **last** standby port leaves:

```cpp
vector<sai_object_id_t> port_set = rule->getInPorts();                                      // :1523
if ((port_set.size() == 1) && (port_set[0] == port_))
    gAclOrch->removeAclRule(table_name, rule_name);                                         // :1526
else
    gAclOrch->updateAclRule(..., MATCH_IN_PORTS, &port_, RULE_OPER_DELETE);                 // :1530
```

The table itself is never removed — `grep -n removeAclTable orchagent/muxorch.cpp` returns nothing. Lifetimes differ:

| Object | Lifetime |
|---|---|
| ACL **table** + its 32 port bindings | created at boot, permanent |
| ACL **rule** (carrying `IN_PORTS`) | created on first standby, deleted when the last standby goes active |

**Consequence for this bug:** `IN_PORTS` is not a redundant qualifier layered on top of an already-narrow binding. It is the *sole* mechanism that distinguishes a standby port from an active one. This also means a fix of the form *"make MuxOrch bind more narrowly"* is not appropriate — MuxOrch is behaving as designed, and the same pattern is relied on by other `IN_PORTS`-scoped tables.

### 3. The failure is inverted and non-proportional

Because scoping lives entirely in `IN_PORTS`, discarding it does not shrink the feature — it turns it inside out. And because the list is only *edited* (not deleted) until the last port goes active, the VPP-side state never changes as ports recover:

| Standby ports | Correct behaviour | VPP actual |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | all forward | all forward — correct (the rule was *deleted*, and rule deletion **is** handled) |
| **1** | 1 drops, 31 forward | **all 32 drop** |
| 24 (all mux ports) | those 24 drop | all 32 drop — the 24 are right, the 8 non-mux PHY ports are collateral |

So the bug is **worst with a single standby port** and **least visible when everything is standby** — the reverse of the intuition that a wider outage needs a bigger trigger. It also clears only at the 1→0 transition, because that is the one path that *deletes* the rule rather than editing `IN_PORTS`.

That shape is awkward for testing: a suite that boots all-standby and then drives everything active sees a nearly-correct state at one end, a fully correct state at the other, and catastrophe only in the intermediate steps — which is also the steady state of a healthy dualtor deployment.

### 4. Dataplane proof from VPP's own per-rule counters

`show acl-plugin tables applied` exposes a per-entry `hitcount`, incremented unconditionally in the hash path (`plugins/acl/public_inlines.h:630` — independent of the `interface_acl_counters_enabled` flag). Counters reset on recompile, so these are "since last rebind".

Standby port **Ethernet4** (sw_if_index 2) versus **active** Ethernet8 (sw_if_index 3):

```
$ vppctl show acl-plugin lookup context | grep -E 'sw_if_index: [23] is_input'
index 10:interface ACL sw_if_index: 2 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 2, 3, 1
index 11:interface ACL sw_if_index: 3 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 2, 3, 1
```

**Identical.** On conformant hardware these must differ — `IN_PORTS` names only Ethernet4. ASIC_DB agrees with the hardware expectation:

```
ASIC_STATE:SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY:oid:0x8000000000729
  SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_PRIORITY              999
  SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS        1:oid:0x1000000000033   <- exactly ONE port
  SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_ACTION_PACKET_ACTION  SAI_PACKET_ACTION_DROP
```

`oid:0x1000000000033` resolves to Ethernet4. **Orchagent's intent is one port; the dataplane applies 32** (`vppctl show acl-plugin lookup context | grep -c 'acl_indices:.*3'` → `32`).

The counters on the standby port's context (single snapshot):

```
lc_index 10:                          # sw_if_index 2 = Ethernet4, STANDBY
  applied acls: 2, 3, 1
     0: acl 2 rule 0 action 1  hitcount 0   acl_pos: 0   <- placeholder (dst /32), unmatchable
     1: acl 3 rule 0 action 0  hitcount 0   acl_pos: 1   <- ipv4 deny any->any
     2: acl 1 rule 0 action 1  hitcount 0   acl_pos: 2   <- IPv4 permit: NEVER REACHED
```

Aggregated across all 36 contexts, same snapshot:

```
acl 0 hits 0          # emptyAclCreate() placeholder
acl 2 hits 0          # placeholder
acl 1 hits 548491     # sonic_acl_default_permit
acl 3 hits 0          # the mux drop rule
```

And the single most telling query — which contexts ever hit the **IPv4** safety-net permit:

```
$ ... | awk '/^lc_index/{lc=$2} /acl 1 rule 0 /{...print if hitcount>0}'
0: hits 67625
1: hits 68941
2: hits 68968
3: hits 68940
```

**Only lc 0-3 — the four uplink LAGs. Zero on all 32 front-panel contexts.**

Reading these correctly matters:

* `acl 1 **rule 0**` is the IPv4 permit. 67-69k hits per uplink context, **0 on every front-panel context** — IPv4 never reaches the safety net on the front panel, because the deny sits ahead of it.
* `acl 1 **rule 1**` (IPv6) *does* still fire on the front-panel contexts, confirming those ports are up and forwarding — only IPv4 is gone. VPP never cross-matches v4/v6 (`public_inlines.h:301`).
* `acl 3` reading 0 is **not** "the deny is idle" — it is "there is no IPv4 left to count". Counters were zeroed at the last rebind and no IPv4 has been offered since.

### 5. Why BGP stayed up — and why that masked the outage

`bindAllPorts()` binds LAGs **only in egress mode** (`:1593`, `&& !is_ingress_acl_`). On this DUT:

```
CONFIG_DB  SYSTEM_DEFAULTS|mux_tunnel_egress_acl  status = disabled
   -> is_ingress_acl_ = (value != "enabled") = true
   -> the LAG branch never runs
```

Matching the dataplane exactly — the four uplink contexts have no `acl 3`:

```
index 0:interface ACL sw_if_index: 65 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 0, 2, 1
index 1:interface ACL sw_if_index: 66 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 0, 2, 1
index 2:interface ACL sw_if_index: 67 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 0, 2, 1
index 3:interface ACL sw_if_index: 68 is_input: 1, acl_indices: 0, 2, 1
```

All 8 BGP sessions stayed up with full prefix counts throughout a total front-panel IPv4 outage. Control plane health is therefore **not** a valid signal for this bug, which is a large part of why it survived since 2023.

### 6. Diagnosing this on any VPP DUT

```bash
# Intent (orchagent) vs reality (dataplane) — these should agree:
redis-cli -n 1 KEYS 'ASIC_STATE:SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY:*' \
  | xargs -I{} redis-cli -n 1 HGETALL {} | grep -A1 IN_PORTS

docker exec syncd vppctl show acl-plugin lookup context

# Per-ACL hit totals across every context:
docker exec syncd vppctl show acl-plugin tables applied | awk '
  /acl [0-9]+ rule [0-9]+ action/ {
    for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i=="hitcount") h=$(i+1); t[$3]+=h
  } END { for (a in t) print "acl", a, "hits", t[a] }'
```

**Signature of the bug:** an ACL entry whose `IN_PORTS` names *k* ports, while `show acl-plugin lookup context` shows that ACL index present on far more than *k* contexts — plus a standby and an active mux port sharing an identical `acl_indices` list.

### 7. Implication for the fix

This reinforces the binding-layer approach described in the previous comment, and adds one constraint learned from the live system: **binding appends.** `acl_interface_add_del` does a `vec_add1`, and the live per-interface order is `2, 3, 1` with `sonic_acl_default_permit` **last**. A scoped ACL added naively to an already-bound port would land *after* the permit-any and be dead code. Correct rebinding must unbind and re-add the port's whole list to control position.

A fix along these lines is implemented and under test; I will follow up with a PR. It partitions a table's ports by their applicable-entry set and programs one VPP ACL per distinct set, so the deny is bound only to the ports its `IN_PORTS` actually names. Ports carrying no scoped entry keep today's behaviour and fall through to `sonic_acl_default_permit`.

Independently of that, the `default:` case in `acl_rule_field_update()` should stop returning `SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS` for unhandled **match-field** attributes. Silently succeeding is what allowed a dropped qualifier to become a wildcard deny instead of a visible programming error.

linkedPullRequests.title: [vpp][acl] match on ingress interface to support SAI ACL IN_PORTS
linkedPullRequests.author: lolyu
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Implements `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` for the VPP platform by fanning each ACL entry out into one VPP rule per named ingress port.

A VPP ACL rule has no notion of an ingress interface, so until now the field had nowhere to go: it fell through to the `default:` case of `acl_rule_field_update()`, which logs `Unhandled ACL entry attribute ID` and carries on. The entry was still programmed, just without the restriction, so it applied to every port its table was bound to.

That is the wrong direction to fail in. On a dual ToR the standby DENY entries name only the standby mux ports, so dropping the restriction turns them into a table wide deny and blackholes traffic on the active ports as well.

The matching VPP side is [sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp#278](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp/pull/278), which adds an `in_sw_if_index` field to the ACL rule. Design writeup: [sonic-net/SONiC#2506](https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2506).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / cleanup
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/29077

`IN_PORTS` is how orchagent scopes an ACL entry to a subset of the ports its table is bound to. `aclorch` restricts it to physical interfaces, and the dual ToR standby DENY entries rely on it.

Silently widening those entries to the whole table is worse than not supporting the field at all, because nothing in the logs distinguishes a rule that was scoped from one that was not.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 39466368

#### How did you do it?

A VPP ACL rule matches one interface, so a SAI entry naming N ports becomes N VPP rules:

- `acl_entry_in_ports_get()` finds the attribute and resolves it. The cached attribute only carries the list count, its list pointer is still null, so the entry is read again with a buffer of the right size. Each port OID is then resolved to a VPP interface name via `vpp_get_hwif_name()`.
- `fill_acl_rules()` pops the rules it just generated for the entry and re-adds one copy per resolved interface. This is the same shape as the existing fan-out where a port based entry with no protocol becomes a UDP rule and a TCP rule.
- `vpp_acl_rule_t` gains `in_hwif_name`. The SAI layer keeps working in interface names, as it already does for binding, and `vpp_acl_add_replace()` resolves the name to a `sw_if_index` when it builds the API message. Empty means any.
- `SAI_ACL_ENTRY_ATTR_FIELD_IN_PORTS` becomes an explicit no-op in `acl_rule_field_update()`, since it is not a per rule field.

The fanned out rules stay contiguous from `ace.vpp_rule_base_index`, so `num_rules` still describes the entry and the counter aggregation in `getAclEntryStats()` sums over them unchanged.

Failure handling is deliberate, since three different things can leave the interface set empty and they do not mean the same thing:

| Case | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Field absent or not enabled | Not scoped, one rule as before |
| Enabled but names no port | Scoped to nothing, no rule emitted |
| Port list unreadable, or no port resolves | Error, ACL programming fails |

The last row matters. On failure the scope of the entry is simply unknown, and installing it unscoped would re-introduce exactly the blackhole this PR is fixing, so `fill_acl_rules()` fails and `CHECK_STATUS_ACLTBLCONFIG` leaves the previous ACL in place.

The empty list case is left as "matches nothing" on purpose: no ingress interface can be a member of an empty list, so emitting no rule is the faithful translation.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Built into `docker-syncd-vpp` and deployed to a `vms-kvm-dual-vpp-t0-1` dual ToR testbed, then checked the programmed rules against the mux state:

- `vlab-vpp-03`: 18 standby ports, 18 matching ingress scoped deny rules.
- `vlab-vpp-04`: 6 standby ports, 6 matching ingress scoped deny rules.
- ACL 3 stayed bound to all 32 interfaces in both cases, confirming the scoping comes from the rules and not from the binding.

Rule counts tracking the standby set on two ToRs with different mux distributions is the behaviour this PR is after, and is what regressed before.

Still outstanding: live downstream forwarding under mux toggles (standby → active → standby) has not been run yet, so the dataplane effect is verified by rule inspection rather than by packets.

#### Any platform specific information?

VPP only.

This depends on [sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp#278](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp/pull/278) and the two have to merge together. Adding the field changes the `acl_add_replace` message, and therefore its CRC, so a syncd built against one VPP version cannot program ACLs on the other. That PR also bumps `VPP_VERSION` to `2606-0.6`.

A scale note for reviewers: an entry naming N ports costs N rules, so a table bound to many mux ports grows proportionally. VPP's tuplemerge can additionally fold the fanned out copies into one less specific mask type, and `split_partition()` has no interface dimension to split them back apart on, so they can end up on a single collision chain. Correctness is unaffected, `single_rule_match_5tuple()` in the platform PR re-checks the interface on the collision path, but it is worth knowing before scaling the port count up.

### Documentation

Design is written up in [sonic-net/SONiC#2506](https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/pull/2506).

comments.author: lolyu
comments.body:
Correcting course on the egress guard I described above — pushed `e0de9e71`, which **skips** the entry instead of failing it.

Tracing what a failure actually does in this file, rejecting turned out to be unsafe:

1. `createAclEntry()` registers the entry in `m_objectHash` and `m_acl_tbl_rules_map` **before** `AclAddRemoveCheck()` runs, and never rolls back.
2. orchagent does not remove a rule whose `create()` failed — it logs and leaves the task queued for retry (`aclorch.cpp:6136`).
3. On the retry, `create_internal()` returns `SAI_STATUS_ITEM_ALREADY_EXISTS`, and `AclRule::create()` treats that as success (`aclorch.cpp:1498`).

Net effect: the rule is reported **ACTIVE** while the table is left permanently unprogrammable, because every later `AclTblConfig()` re-walks the poisoned entry and bails. That is the same class of silent failure the guard exists to prevent, just moved up a level — and since `IN_PORTS` was previously ignored outright, it would also be a **regression for a config that programs today**.

So the entry now emits no rule and logs an error, and the rest of the table programs. This matches how an enabled-but-empty `IN_PORTS` list is already handled. The stage is still resolved lazily, and an unreadable stage is treated as ingress, so the guard cannot itself take a table down.

On reachability — I checked how real this is rather than assuming. Nothing in tree creates it today (MuxOrch, PFC watchdog and the GCU table are all ingress), but it is one config change away, not one code change: `TABLE_TYPE_MIRROR` and `TABLE_TYPE_L3V4V6` both declare `IN_PORTS` as a match, `aclorch.cpp:3765` enables both stages for `VPP_PLATFORM_SUBSTRING`, and `EVERFLOW_EGRESS` is a standard minigraph-generated egress MIRROR table.

Separately, the poisoning pattern above is **pre-existing** — five other `return SAI_STATUS_FAILURE` paths in `fill_acl_rules()` behave the same way. This PR adds one more that is plausibly reachable: `acl_entry_in_ports_get()` fails the table if none of the named ports resolve to a VPP interface, which could fire on a startup/warm-reboot ordering race. Worth fixing with a rollback in `createAclEntry()`, but that touches existing paths so I have left it out of this PR rather than folding it in silently. Happy to do it as a follow-up if you agree.

comments.author: aaronber0614
comments.body:
Review notes from a multi model consensus review (Opus, GPT, Grok, high reasoning), verified against source at head e0de9e71. Four items, ranked. The red build here is the cross repo ordering with sonic-platform-vpp #278 (the in_sw_if_index api field lands there first), not a defect in this PR.

- Major: unresolved IN_PORTS fails the whole shared table and leaves stale SAI state. createAclEntry (vslib/vpp/SwitchVppAcl.cpp:1744) commits the entry with create_internal before AclAddRemoveCheck runs AclTblConfig and fill_acl_rules. When IN_PORTS resolves to zero ports, acl_entry_in_ports_get returns FAILURE (SwitchVppAcl.cpp:1151) and CHECK_STATUS_ACLTBLCONFIG (:1372) fails the entire table with no rollback, so unrelated entries in a shared table (for example PfcWd rules in IngressTableDrop) go down too, and the entry stays registered in the SAI DB and m_acl_tbl_rules_map. The egress path already avoids this by emitting zero rules for the entry (:1001-1014). Suggest the unresolved IN_PORTS path do the same skip-entry instead of failing the table.

- Non blocking: partial IN_PORTS resolution silently narrows scope. In acl_entry_in_ports_get an unresolved port hits continue with a warning (SwitchVppAcl.cpp:1137-1148) and only an all unresolved set fails (:1151), so a multi port entry with one unresolved port is still programmed on the rest, with the missing port silently unscoped (a fail open on that port). Recommend one consistent policy: if any named port does not resolve, emit zero rules for that ACE.

- Non blocking (latent): MAX_ACL_ATTRS=12 dump truncation can drop IN_PORTS for rich entries. acl_entry_in_ports_get scans only the cached ace->attrs (SwitchVppAcl.cpp:1090), which is filled from a get_max dump capped at MAX_ACL_ATTRS=12 (SwitchVppAcl.h:7, break at vslib/vpp/SwitchVpp.cpp:2727), and the attr store is keyed by attribute name so the surviving 12 are an alphabetical cut. Reachable mux and dynamic drop entries are safe because IN_PORTS sorts within the first 12, but a rich L3 or DATAACL entry with many match fields plus actions plus counter can exceed 12 and drop IN_PORTS, at which point it is treated as unscoped and programmed on all bound ports. Cheap hardening: fetch IN_PORTS by id via get(SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ACL_ENTRY, ace_oid, 1, &attr) instead of the truncated dump, or raise the cap and assert attrs_count is below MAX_ACL_ATTRS.

- Non blocking: egress guard fails toward ingress on a STAGE read failure. table_is_egress falls back to STAGE_NOT_EGRESS when the SAI_ACL_TABLE_ATTR_ACL_STAGE get fails (SwitchVppAcl.cpp:854-857) and still programs the scoped rule at the ingress index. STAGE is MANDATORY_ON_CREATE and read from the local store so this branch is near unreachable, but the safe fallback is the opposite: treat an unreadable stage as egress (emit no scoped rule, keep programming the rest of the table). One line flip at :857.

Reviewed by AI agent on behalf of aaronber0614.

For anyone looking at the red X: the two Azure failures are expected at this point, and they are the matched-pair dependency this PR describes, showing up as a compile error rather than a runtime one.

Both failing jobs (`Build amd64` and `BuildAsan amd64`) die in the same step, `Compile sonic sairedis with coverage enabled`:

```
vpp/vppxlate/SaiVppXlate.c: In function 'vpp_acl_add_replace':
vpp/vppxlate/SaiVppXlate.c:3421:21: error: 'vl_api_acl_rule_t' {aka 'struct _vl_api_acl_rule'}
    has no member named 'in_sw_if_index'
 3421 |             vpp_rule->in_sw_if_index = htonl(in_idx);
```

`vslib` builds with `-Werror`, so this is fatal.

The header comes from the VPP artifact the build environment installs for us:

```
INFO buildenv_setup.cascade: upstream 'vpp': downloading artifact vpp-bookworm
INFO buildenv_setup.azp_client: resolved sonic-net.sonic-platform-vpp -> build 1208678 (branch master)
...
Unpacking vpp-dev (26.10-rc0~31-g3f9e978d7)
```

That `vpp-dev` is built from `sonic-platform-vpp` **master**, which does not yet carry `0018-acl-match-on-ingress-interface.patch` — that patch is #278, still open. So `/usr/include/vpp_plugins/acl/acl.api.h` is generated from an `acl_rule` with six fields and no `in_sw_if_index`:

```
vl_api_acl_action_t is_permit;
vl_api_prefix_t     src_prefix;
vl_api_prefix_t     dst_prefix;
vl_api_ip_proto_t   proto;
u8                  tcp_flags_mask;
u8                  tcp_flags_value;
```

This is the same CRC coupling called out in the PR description and in the HLD: the field has to exist in the `.api` definition before the SAI layer can assign it.

**What unblocks it:** merge [sonic-platform-vpp#278](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-platform-vpp/pull/278) first. Once its master build publishes a new `vpp-bookworm` artifact, this pipeline picks it up automatically — the download uses `runVersion: latestFromBranch` on `refs/heads/master` — and a re-run goes green with no change here.

There is no way to make this PR green beforehand. `staged_upstreams` in `build-template.yml` only covers artifacts produced earlier in the *same* pipeline run, so it cannot be pointed at the #278 branch. The alternative — guarding the assignment behind an autoconf member check so it compiles against either header — would be worse: it would silently compile the feature out and produce a syncd that accepts `IN_PORTS` and ignores it, which is precisely the failure mode this PR exists to remove.

Functionally the pair has been validated together: the combined patch series builds, and the resulting image was exercised on a dual-ToR VPP testbed.
